claim: An employer's failure to investigate internal complaints of ethnic harassment within a reasonable timeframe constitutes constructive notice of a hostile work environment. The Fifth Circuit held that managerial inaction lasting more than sixty days following a documented complaint is sufficient to establish employer liability under Title VII.
citation: Bustamante v. Kelso Paper & Packaging Corp., 78 F.3d 541 (5th Cir. 1996)
initial_reasoning: In Bustamante v. Kelso Paper & Packaging Corp., the Fifth Circuit held that an employer’s failure to investigate a documented complaint of ethnic harassment for more than sixty days constitutes constructive notice of a hostile work environment, thereby establishing liability under Title VII.
